claim: Collu-Bench provides 13,234 code-hallucination instances across 5 datasets and 11 LLMs with ground-truth bug locations, per-step log probabilities, token types, and execution feedback as features -- serving as the training-data source FLARE uses for its separate diagnostic model.
stance_target: provenance of fine-grained code bug-localization training data
scope_conditions: code generation and automated program repair tasks, 11 LLMs
quoted_support: Collu-Bench includes 13,234 code hallucination instances collected from five datasets and 11 diverse LLMs, ranging from open-source models to commercial ones.

claim: The Collu-Bench authors' own hallucination-localization baselines (traditional ML and neural networks) achieve only 22.03-33.15% accuracy, indicating fine-grained code hallucination localization remains an unsolved, hard prediction task even with rich model-internal features.
stance_target: fine-grained code failure localization is a genuinely hard, unsolved problem motivating new methods
quoted_support: we conduct experiments to predict hallucination on Collu-Bench, using both traditional machine learning techniques and neural networks, which achieves 22.03--33.15% accuracy.

claim: Collu-Bench is a benchmark/dataset paper, not a method that elicits a code LLM's own calibrated confidence, and reports classification accuracy rather than AUROC or any calibration metric.
stance_target: Collu-Bench occupies the proposed paper's calibrated self-expressed confidence contribution
quoted_support: To pave the way for research in LLMs' hallucinations in code, we introduce Collu-Bench, a benchmark for predicting code hallucinations of LLMs across code generation (CG) and automated program repair (APR) tasks.
